title: Open the story
description: Give your adventure a setting and a surprise.

tasks.title: Your story starts with one instruction
tasks.body: A program is a set of instructions. Python follows these instructions from top to bottom. Use print() to display words on the screen.
tasks.detail: Put text inside matching quotation marks, then put that string inside the parentheses. Use lowercase print. The quotation marks do not appear in the output.

tasks.code:
print("You arrive at a moonlit castle.")
print("A tiny dragon opens the gate.")
tasks.output:
You arrive at a moonlit castle.
A tiny dragon opens the gate.
tasks.note: Each print() adds a new line. Two instructions give you two lines of story.

tasks.question: Which message appears first?
tasks.why: Python runs the first print statement before the second. Swapping the code lines swaps the messages.

tasks.prompt: Change the dragon into a different creature. Keep the matching quotes and parentheses, then run your story.

Write two print statements with two different story messages: first a place, then a surprise. The check makes sure you print two different messages that use words; whether they make a good scene is up to you.
tasks.starter:
# Describe a location with print()
# On the next line, print an unexpected event
hints: You need two print() lines: the first describes a place, the second something unexpected.
Check each line: lowercase print, then parentheses, with your message inside matching quotes.
A pattern to complete: print("You wake up in ___.") Then add a second print() with your surprise.

error_hints.text: Every opening quote needs a closing quote, and every ( needs a ). Check the end of each line.
print is all lowercase, and words need quotes around them. Without quotes, Python reads words as names.
Each message needs words, like the name of a place or something that happens.
Keep your first line as it is, and make the second one about something else that happens.

similar_example.note: One print() shows one line of text. Your challenge uses two, with your own words.

messages.message: Write two print statements with nonempty messages: one location, then one surprise.
Use words for each message: first a place, then something unexpected. Numbers or punctuation on their own don't tell a story.
Both lines say the same thing. Change the second one into a surprise.
Fill in the ___ from the hint with your own words.
That's the example from the card. Make it your own: change the place and the surprise.
That line comes straight from a hint. Change it into your own words.
Python printed your two different messages in order. Read them back: does the first set the scene and the second surprise you? That part is your call.
